h1:
Prachuap & Hua Hin Food
Seafood, Mackerel & Pineapple to Try
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan is a long province running down the Gulf coast, from Hua Hin all the way to Bang Saphan, and you can find fresh seafood in just about every district. Three things really stand out: bayside seafood landed off the boats each morning, Prachuap Bay mackerel that locals say is short but full of fat, and pineapple grown across the whole province until it became the local souvenir. We've pulled together the dishes and the spots people around here actually go to, so you can plan before your trip.

blocks.html: If you drive south from Bangkok, Prachuap Khiri Khan is one of the first provinces where you catch the sea air. Hua Hin sits at the top of the province and is the seaside town with the most food and the most variety. The town of Prachuap itself, further south, is quieter, but the seafood is fresh and prices run cheaper. This guide is split into three parts to give you the full picture: seafood, mackerel and dried seafood, and pineapple souvenirs.

Seafood is the heart of eating around here. Fishing boats come in during the morning, so everything is fresh — prawns, shellfish, crab, squid, right up to big fish. The places locals favour usually aren't fancy, but the catch is fresh and the price is fair. We've picked spots by the actual neighbourhoods they're in.

items.name: Rab Lom — on Prachuap Bay
items.blurb: A seaside spot in Prachuap town with a good breeze and easy seating, and one people often recommend when you come into town. The dishes everyone orders are stir-fried sea snail with chilli, sun-dried squid, and spicy blood cockle salad.
items.meta: Mueang district, on Prachuap Bay · lunch–dinner

items.name: Kon Kin Pla — Khlong Wan
items.blurb: A local fish restaurant in the Khlong Wan area, south of Prachuap town, known for fresh fish and simple home-style cooking. It's the place locals mention when they want straightforward sea fish that isn't over-seasoned.

items.name: Krua Chom Whale — Kui Buri
items.blurb: A seaside spot in the Kui Buri area, between Hua Hin and Prachuap town, with a setting right on the water. Favourites are tamarind-fried fish and stir-fried seafood — a good stop on the way south.

items.name: Chao Lay Seafood — Hua Hin
items.blurb: A long-running, well-known seafood spot in Hua Hin. A common order is grilled scallops with garlic butter, and the catch is fresh with an easy-to-walk location in central Hua Hin.
items.meta: Hua Hin district, in town · lunch–dinner

items.name: Sopha Seafood — Hua Hin
items.blurb: A Hua Hin seafood spot that buys from local fishermen, so the stock changes daily with whatever the boats bring in. Better suited to people who want the fresh daily catch rather than a fixed menu.

items.name: Krua Je Maew — Pak Nam Pran
items.blurb: A spot in the Pak Nam Pran area (Pran Buri) that reviewers praise for bold, well-seasoned flavours. The standout is sour curry with fish roe, and travellers on the Pran Buri side stop here often.
items.meta: Pran Buri district, Pak Nam Pran · lunch–dinner

items.name: Hua Hin Fishing Pier — fresh seafood
items.blurb: Not a single restaurant but the fishing-pier area in Hua Hin itself. In the morning fresh seafood comes off the boats; you can take in the sea view and buy fresh catch, and a few spots grill it for you on the spot.
items.meta: Hua Hin district, fishing pier · morning–late morning

items.name: Hua Hin Night Market — grilled seafood
items.blurb: A night market on Dechanuchit Road, roughly 300 metres long, open from evening into the small hours. The grilled-seafood section has several stalls in a row at fair prices — ideal for a dinner where you walk and graze, ordering one thing at a time.

blocks.title: Tips for ordering seafood
blocks.html: Most beachfront places price fresh seafood by weight. Before you order, ask the price per kilo and ask to see the actual catch — it saves confusion when the bill comes. Crab and tiger prawns are usually the priciest, while squid and shellfish tend to be better value.

blocks.text: Prachuap Bay mackerel and dried seafood

blocks.html: Prachuap Bay is a mackerel ground locals take pride in. People around here say the bay's mackerel isn't big but is full of fat with firm flesh, and it's good steamed or fried. Beyond fresh mackerel, dried and preserved seafood is both a dish and a souvenir you'll find across the province.

items: Steamed / fried mackerel — found at fresh markets across Prachuap town and Hua Hin. Eaten with shrimp-paste chilli dip, it's a home-style meal you never tire of.
Sun-dried squid — a Gulf coast specialty; fry it and it turns sweet and springy. Buy it raw to fry at home, or order it at a restaurant.
Local shrimp paste & fish sauce — around Khlong Wan and Bang Saphan they make their own shrimp paste, richer than the supermarket kind, a good souvenir for anyone who cooks.
Dried shrimp / salted fish — sold at Chatchai Market in Hua Hin and the Prachuap fresh market. Pick a stall with a queue so the stock keeps turning over and stays fresh.

blocks.html: If you want to see real fishing-town life, Chatchai Market in Hua Hin is a morning market that's been part of the town for over 80 years, with fresh seafood every day. Hua Hin locals do their shopping here, and there are old-school coffee shops like Jek Pia for a traditional breakfast.

Prachuap Khiri Khan grows pineapple across the whole province; along Phetkasem Road through Prachuap you'll see pineapple fields stretching out on both sides. The pineapple here is firm and juicy-sweet — eaten fresh and also processed into souvenirs.

items.name: Fresh pineapple
items.blurb: Sold at roadside stalls and fresh markets. Pick a fruit that feels heavy, with big eyes and a good smell — far cheaper than buying it in Bangkok.

items.name: Pineapple jam / dried pineapple
items.blurb: A popular souvenir that keeps well and travels easily. Find it at souvenir shops in town and at roadside rest stops.

items.name: Pineapple dishes
items.blurb: Many seafood spots cook with pineapple — like fried sea bass with pineapple sauce, the sweet-sour cutting through anything rich.

items.name: Fresh pineapple juice
items.blurb: Markets and cafes press it fresh. Refreshing on a hot day and only a few baht.

items: Hai Piang (Hua Hin) — an old Chinese restaurant in Hua Hin going back more than 60 years, with home-style Chinese dishes that longtime Hua Hin locals know well.
Hua Hin cafes — Hua Hin has plenty of cafes, both beachfront and in town, good for an afternoon break between meals.
Steamed rice-skin dumplings & Thai sweets at Chatchai Market — a Thai breakfast Hua Hin locals actually eat. Go early while the selection is still full.

faq.q: What food is Prachuap Khiri Khan known for?
faq.a: Three things come to mind: bayside seafood (prawns, shellfish, crab and squid fresh off the boats), Prachuap Bay mackerel that's short but full of fat, and sweet pineapple grown across the whole province until it became the local souvenir.

faq.q: Where's a good place to eat seafood in Prachuap town?
faq.a: In town there are bayside spots like Rab Lom on Prachuap Bay, while the Khlong Wan area to the south has local fish restaurants like Kon Kin Pla. Both neighbourhoods are fresher and cheaper than the Hua Hin side.

faq.q: Is eating in Hua Hin different from Prachuap town?
faq.a: Quite different. Hua Hin has more food and more variety — a night market, in-town seafood, cafes and international restaurants. Prachuap town and further south are quieter, but the seafood is fresher and cheaper.

faq.q: What time does the Hua Hin night market open?
faq.a: It runs from the evening, around 17:00, until roughly midnight every day, on Dechanuchit Road. The grilled-seafood section has several stalls in a row — ideal for a dinner where you walk and graze.

faq.q: Which Prachuap pineapple souvenir should I buy?
faq.a: If you'll eat it right away, buy fresh pineapple from roadside stalls and pick a fruit that feels heavy and smells good. If you're carrying it far, go for pineapple jam or dried pineapple, which keep well and don't bruise.
